sentences.text: Caulkicephalus is a genus of anhanguerid pterosaur found on the Isle of Wight off the coast of England.
The combined length of the preserved snout fragments is 290 mm.
A crest is present on top of the snout, which does not have a rounded tip.
A damaged posterior cranial fragment shows the base of a parietal crest on top, which likely pointed backward.
The fourth tooth pair matched the first in size, while the fifth, sixth, and seventh pairs were notably smaller, less than half the size, a feature referenced in the species name.
The genus name combines "Caulkhead", a traditional nickname for Wight island residents, with the Greek word kephale meaning "head".
The species name trimicrodon means "three small teeth", referring to its dentition.
David Martill estimated that Caulkicephalus had a wingspan of nearly five meters.
Bone fragments of an unknown pterosaur were discovered between 1995 and 2003 at the Yaverland locality near Sandown.
The fossils were found in brown clay from the Wessex Formation of the Wealden Group, dating to the Early Cretaceous (Barremian), approximately 130 million years ago.
The genus Caulkicephalus was named and described in 2005 by Lorna Steel, David Martill, David Unwin, and John Winch.
The holotype consists of three roughly contiguous pieces from the front of the snout.
A constriction in the snout with larger teeth at the broad end, known as a "prey grab," is interpreted as an adaptation for catching slippery prey like fish.
Small teeth were located in a compressed area of the snout ending in a wide tip with large teeth, forming a "trap" generally believed to be an adaptation for catching elusive prey like fish.
The presence of land plant debris in the fossil layer suggests Caulkicephalus may have inhabited a more terrestrial environment.
The fossil layer contained terrestrial plant residues rather than marine sediments, suggesting a possible terrestrial habitat.
The type species of the genus Caulkicephalus is Caulkicephalus trimicrodon.
Caulkicephalus is classified in the class Reptilia.
Studies in 2019 reassigned Caulkicephalus to the family Anhangueridae, subfamily Anhanguerinae, as a sister taxon to Guidraco and Ludodactylus.
The describers assigned Caulkicephalus to the family Ornithocheiridae due to the narrowing in the middle of the snout.
The snout crest indicated membership in the broader group Ornithocheiroidea, while the parietal crest was suggested as a shared trait of the narrower group Euornithocheira.
The parent group for Caulkicephalus is Ornithocheiridae.
Caulkicephalus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 million years ago.
The time range for Caulkicephalus is the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
The original describers assigned Caulkicephalus to the family Ornithocheiridae based on the narrowing in the middle of the snout, a classification later revised.
